record.paper_title: Selected Open Problems in Continuous-Time Quantum Walks
record.context_brief: Non-negative rank of the average mixing matrix
record.original_question: Let G be a graph with average mixing matrix \hat{M}=lim_{T→∞}(1/T)∫_0^T M(t)dt = Σ_r E_r∘E_r. The non-negative rank of a non-negative n×n matrix is the least k for which the matrix factors through non-negative vectors of dimension k. Determine exactly when the non-negative rank of \hat{M} is equal to n, the number of vertices of G.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G be a finite simple graph on n vertices with adjacency matrix A. Write the spectral decomposition A = Σ_{r=0}^{d} λ_r E_r, where E_0, E_1, …, E_d are the orthogonal spectral idempotents of A. The continuous-time quantum walk on G is the family of unitary matrices U(t) = exp(itA), and the associated mixing matrix is M(t) := U(t) ∘ U(−t), where ∘ denotes the Schur (entrywise) product. The average mixing matrix of G is defined as

   M̂ := lim_{T→∞} (1/T) ∫_0^T M(t) dt,

and one has the identity M̂ = Σ_{r=0}^{d} E_r ∘ E_r. In particular, M̂ is a symmetric, doubly stochastic, entrywise non-negative n×n matrix.

For a non-negative matrix N ∈ ℝ^{n×n}, the non-negative rank rank_+(N) is defined to be the smallest integer k such that there exist non-negative vectors u_1, …, u_k, v_1, …, v_k ∈ ℝ^n with N = Σ_{i=1}^{k} u_i v_i^T. One always has rank_+(M̂) ≤ n.

Problem: Characterize exactly the finite simple graphs G on n vertices for which rank_+(M̂) = n.
artifact.category_tag: Average mixing matrices in continuous-time quantum walks
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature on average mixing matrices (Godsil and collaborators, and follow-up works through 2024–2025) studies the (ordinary) rank of M̂ and its combinatorial significance, but no source found provides a characterization of graphs for which the non-negative rank of M̂ equals the number of vertices. The question appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: A New Perspective on the Average Mixing Matrix
status_evidence.snippet: Connections between the rank of the average mixing matrix and automorphisms of the graph are established.
status_evidence.claim: Existing work focuses on the ordinary rank of M̂, not the non-negative rank.

status_evidence.title: Average Mixing in Quantum Walks of Reversible Markov Chains
status_evidence.snippet: Studies spectral and structural properties of average mixing matrices.
status_evidence.claim: Recent literature continues to investigate M̂ but does not resolve the non-negative rank question.

status_evidence.title: Discrete Quantum Walks with Marked Vertices and Their Average Vertex Mixing Matrices
status_evidence.snippet: Derives formulas and bounds for entries of average vertex mixing matrices.
status_evidence.claim: No characterization of when rank_+(M̂) = n is provided in current work.
